layers.title: The codebase
layers.lede: What is in the repository, why each part is there, and what breaks without it.

sections.title: The shape of it
sections.answer: One kernel computes every number; everything else is arranged in rings that depend inward only. A row is one folder, and only its node.toml is written by hand.
sections.body:
**One kernel computes every number.** Everything else is arranged in rings that depend inward only: quantities and portable maths (`vleo-units`), then the kernel of physics and relations (`vleo-core`), then transport (`vleo-bus`), then one crate per subsystem of rows (`vleo-mod-*`), then the faces — the browser daemon, the command line, and the Python, WebAssembly and C bindings. `xtask graph` checks every dependency points inward.

**Every formula lives in `vleo-core::physics` and nowhere else.** A row composes relations from there in a few lines; it never defines one of its own.

**The tree is layers of rows.** Layer 1 is the programme's view, layer 2 the system's, layer 3 the subsystems', and layer 4 is a run. Each subsystem reaches the layer above through exactly one interface row, so *where did this number come from* is answered by walking upward without ever leaving the tree.

**One row is one folder**, under `crates/vleo-mod-<subsystem>/nodes/<row>/`:

`node.toml` — the sheet. The only file written by hand — by a form's intake, or a developer.
`fixtures.toml` — known-good values from outside this code.
`model.rs` — generated, except the numbered slots where the Rust goes.
`contract.rs`, `mod.rs`, `evidence.rs`, `meta.json` — generated.
The row's page is not in the folder: the tool renders it from the sheet when it is opened.

The rules that do not bend, and the developer's loop, are in `AGENTS.md`; the reasoning behind the architecture is in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

sections.title: Every top-level folder
sections.answer: Every folder and file at the top of the repository, and what it holds — checked against the repository both ways.
sections.body: Every folder and file the repository tracks at its top level is below, with what it holds — the list is checked against the repository itself, so nothing is missing from it and nothing in it is gone.

sections.title: Where to read next
sections.answer: Every document under docs/, and what it is for — checked against the folder both ways.
sections.body: Every document under `docs/`, and what it is for. Also checked against the folder, both ways.

layers.title: Reference
layers.lede: Every command, route and setting, and what a row's sheet holds. The commands and routes are held against the programs themselves; the sheet's fields and the reasons its locked fields are locked are read live from the code that enforces them.

sections.title: xtask — the tree's own tool
sections.answer: The project's own tool for the tree: generate, check, take in forms, record and release.
sections.body: `cargo run -p xtask -- <command>`, or `cargo xtask <command>`. `help` prints the same list with each command's reasons.

sections.title: vleo — the engine from the command line
sections.answer: The engine from the command line: run, sweep, compare cases, and read results.
sections.body: `cargo run -p vleo-cli --bin vleo -- <command>`, or `cargo vleo <command>`.

sections.title: HTTP routes
sections.answer: Every route the daemon answers. None writes the repository; the few that save anything save the case or a result, outside it.
sections.body: Served by the daemon on `127.0.0.1`. **None writes the repository.** The few that save anything save the case or a result, both kept outside it under `~/.vleo/`.

sections.title: Settings
sections.answer: The environment variables the tool reads. None is required.
sections.body: Environment variables the tool and its checks read. None is required.

sections.title: What a node form asks
sections.answer: Every question a node form asks and every list it holds, read live from the table the form is built from.
sections.body: Every question a node's form asks and every list it holds — read live from the table the form itself is built from, so this cannot describe a form that no longer exists.

sections.title: What a node form does not change
sections.answer: The fields that move a row in the tree or change who owns it. No form carries them; a developer changes them in a reviewed commit.
sections.body: The fields that move a row in the tree or change who owns it. A node's form does not carry them, so no filled form can change them; a developer does, in a reviewed change. Each one's reason is live, from the rule that refuses them.

commands.name: docs
commands.what: Generate each row's files from its sheet. Never reads another row.

commands.name: assemble
commands.what: The assembly validations, then the index and the page fragments the browser serves.

commands.name: gate
commands.what: The checks, in order. The one that must pass.

commands.name: status
commands.what: Counts by state and subsystem, and what is holding the tree back.

commands.name: active
commands.what: Which rows answer, and for each that does not, whether its own derivation or a row it reads is missing.

commands.name: catalogue
commands.what: What each group publishes to the others: every row another group reads, or that crosses a layer, with its version and every row that reads it — taken from the inputs the sheets declare. `--csv` writes it as a table. The design file carries it too, as its `published` table.

commands.name: impact
commands.what: Which other groups a change to these rows reaches: the rows that read them, theirs, and so on, by group and nearest first. A group named stands for all its rows. `group-intake` prints the same for the nodes a release changes.

commands.name: reach
commands.what: Where each answer goes, and which reach no customer target.

commands.name: gap
commands.what: What every sheet promised and nothing yet covers.

commands.name: graph
commands.what: The three graphs, their sizes, and the check that every crate depends inward.

commands.name: new
commands.what: Start a row from a sibling's shape, with everything that must be re-decided blanked.

commands.name: declare
commands.what: The questions a sheet still has open, and what goes wrong without each.

commands.name: fill
commands.what: Put the Rust for one numbered slot into a row's generated model. `--by` and `--model` record who wrote it, and with what.

commands.name: differential
commands.what: Compare two recorded bodies for the same slot, written by different model families.

commands.name: form
commands.what: A node's form: one self-contained HTML file that explains itself, asks every question the sheet answers, and saves a filled copy. `--new` is the form for a node the design does not have yet. Filled anywhere, by anyone. --example fills orbit_velocity's form with the worked example, only for the pipeline's end-to-end test of the method path; nothing it produces is committed.

commands.name: intake
commands.what: The checker: what a filled node form would change, field by field, and every interface it declares — conflicts and refusals named. `--apply` writes (building a new node in its place), regenerates and gates as one edit, or puts everything back.

commands.name: lesson
commands.what: A row's lesson: `lesson form <node>` writes its form, one HTML file the node engineer fills anywhere, checked as they type by the gate's own lesson check; `lesson check <file>` says what a filled one holds and every reason it would be refused; `lesson apply` writes it as lesson.toml beside the row and gates the row, or puts it back.

commands.name: publish
commands.what: Move a filled, seeded row to published, so its code is generated and its slots can be written. Refuses, naming every reason, while it is not ready.

commands.name: guides
commands.what: Renders the three role guides — docs/roles/user.html, maintainer.html and developer.html — from this manual. Never edited by hand: the pipeline regenerates them and fails when a committed one differs.

commands.name: method
commands.what: Checks a node's method in the method language and runs each of its node engineer's test cases through it: what their code gave, what the method gives, and whether the set is complete — at least three answers and one refusal. The same check the node form runs as the node engineer types, and the gate refuses on.

commands.name: method-wasm
commands.what: Builds the method checker every node form carries — vleo_sheet::method compiled to WebAssembly — into web/method.wasm.gz with the fingerprint of its sources; --check only says whether the committed file is current.

commands.name: group-app
commands.what: Builds the two offline pages a group works in — web/group.html, where the subsystem engineer sets out the nodes and their contracts, issues each node engineer a node file, assembles the files into a release, has it signed and seals it, and web/node.html, where a node engineer fills their node file — each carrying SQLite (web/vendor/sqlite, checked against its recorded hashes) and the database format of groups/schema.sql; and the folder pattern's two documents, docs/GROUP_FOLDER.md and groups/skill/vleo-group-folder/SKILL.md, all from groups/SPEC.toml. --check only says whether the committed four are current.

commands.name: group-intake
commands.what: A group's sealed release taken into the design. The release, written out with `node tools/group_db.mjs --unpack <file.vleo>`, is refused unless every file still gives the fingerprint it was sealed with; then each computed node's pseudocode and results become its node form — its method and test cases, in SI — and go through intake's own check: a conflict with a change made since, a method or results an assistant supplied (a `transcribed` method counts as one unless it names its source and a person who checked the copy), an incomplete de-risking record. `--apply` writes, regenerates and gates each, or puts it back. `--draft` looks at an unsealed release and never applies.

commands.name: group-build
commands.what: Every computed node of a sealed release, once `group-intake --apply` has taken it in, built from its method: `build-node` on each — translated into the kernel, tested on its node engineer's cases, the tests proved to test, the interface checked. A node whose method in the design is not the release's is refused: the release is taken in first.

commands.name: group-test
commands.what: The group tested against its own results, never against the code under test: the design holds the release's isolation results case for case; each node's own tests pass; the group as a whole, run through the engine, gives `results/group.csv`; and both ends of every range the group declares answer or refuse by name — never NaN, never a crash. The report goes to `target/group/<group>-<version>/group-test.csv`.

commands.name: group-deliver
commands.what: The test application for the group: the kit, built from this commit with their release in it, beside `DELIVERY.toml` — which release, which seal, which commit, which nodes — `DELIVERY.md`, what to try, and the group-test report. Refused until `group-test` has passed, and from uncommitted changes unless `--uncommitted` says the checkout is a throwaway. The group answers accepted, or changes.

commands.name: group-accept
commands.what: The group's answer to its test application, recorded. The subsystem engineer writes it on the group application's Delivery & acceptance page, beside their sealed release; it names the delivery by its SHA-256, the commit it was built from and the release's fingerprint. An answer of accepted, saying what was tried and given by a person, is committed to `acceptances/<group>-<version>.toml` on the branch `group/<group>-<version>` — refused if anything but these records changed since the delivered commit. An answer of changes is never recorded: its note is printed, to take back into the group's work. `--verify` is the pipeline's check on a group branch.

commands.name: group-export
commands.what: Writes one group's folder in the pattern of groups/SPEC.toml from every sheet in the group — its nodes, inputs, plain words, theory, assumptions, evidence and sources — for the group to start from. It invents nothing: a pseudocode, the group's own results and its pictures are left for the group, and the group application lists them. `--all` writes every group that owns a node, each in its own folder, with GROUPS.csv beside them; `node tools/group_db.mjs --all <dir>` then makes each into its database files and READY.csv, what each group still needs.

commands.name: rerun
commands.what: Runs each node engineer's own code again on the cases recorded from it and says whether it still gives them: Python directly, MATLAB and Octave through Octave where it is installed. Code in any other language is kept and read, not rerun, and it says so; `--require` fails instead, for a pipeline that installed the runners.

commands.name: build-node
commands.what: Builds a node from its method, stage by stage, stopping at the first that fails: the method on its node engineer's cases; the translation into the kernel; the node's tests — the node engineer's cases and the translation against the method; the node engineer's code rerun; a mutation the tests must catch; and only then the node in the tree.

commands.name: migration
commands.what: Says which computed rows still need a method, by owner, and with --forms writes each one's node form into <dir>/<owner>/ ready to send. It writes no method: each comes from the node's owner, on the node's form, through take like any other change.

commands.name: explain
commands.what: Where a command sits in a node's journey, what it reads, writes and checks, how to undo it, its steps and where its code is — from the one table docs/PIPELINE.md is written from. With no command, the whole journey.

commands.name: why
commands.what: A node's history in one place: every recorded version and who made it, the commits that changed it, its approvals, how its code came to be, and its gate, run now.

commands.name: trace
commands.what: The last run's trace from target/xtask-trace/ — every command that writes leaves one, the newest 50 kept — or the last of one command, or --list every one kept.

commands.name: pipeline
commands.what: Write docs/PIPELINE.md from the pipeline table; --check only says whether it is current.

commands.name: take
commands.what: Takes a filled node form in: checks it, and if it cannot be taken writes `<form>.returned.txt` to send back and changes nothing; otherwise puts it on its own branch `form/<author>/<node>` from a fresh `maintainer`, applies it, regenerates, gates, tests, commits naming the node engineer and pushes. The push builds the node engineer's preview.

commands.name: preview
commands.what: Where the current form branch's preview build is, and what to do with it. Every push to a form branch builds one by itself.

commands.name: approve
commands.what: Records the node engineer's approval of a preview — the file the preview saves when they press Approve. Refused unless it is for the build of exactly what is on the branch now. `--verify <branch>` is the same check, as the pipeline runs it.

commands.name: queue
commands.what: Every form branch and every group branch, and where each stands: not pushed; waiting for the node engineer's approval, or the group's acceptance of its test application; approved or accepted and ready to merge; or merged.

commands.name: ship
commands.what: Cuts a release from main on its own branch `release/<version>`: the de-risking narrative, the version stamp, regeneration, the gate and the tests, one commit, pushed — and prints the tag commands for after the merge.

commands.name: readers
commands.what: The docs folder for readers: every row's page — the tool's own generated page — and every lesson, read with no tool running, from a shared drive or an internal web server. A lesson's widgets are answered by the engine compiled for the browser (crates/vleo-kernel-wasm), on the declared values; a row that reads reference data refuses there by name. Written to target/readers, or --out; nothing committed.

commands.name: design
commands.what: design.vleo: the tree the tool reads — every node folder with its sheet, fixtures and page, the layers, the cases and the source list — written into one SQLite file, each file whole with its SHA-256. The kit carries it in place of the folders and the daemon reads it as it reads them, so the pages are the same byte for byte. Default target/design.vleo; nothing committed.

commands.name: design
commands.what: A design file held to the tree: each file against its SHA-256, all of them against the fingerprint, and every file against the folders it was written from. Prints the differences and fails on any.

commands.name: kit
commands.what: The tool as each person gets it: the two release-built programs beside exactly the files they read — the design among them as one file, design.vleo — with START_HERE.md and VERSION (and start.sh off Windows, where the daemon ships as Start VLEO.exe), in dist/vleo-<version>/. Zip it and share it; see docs/SHARING.md. --files-only leaves the programs out: the files the Python package carries.

commands.name: derisk
commands.what: Write the de-risking narrative — docs/DERISK_NARRATIVE.md and docs/derisking.csv — from every node's `[[version]]` record and the risk register. Generated, never edited.

commands.name: release
commands.what: Stamp every node version still marked `next` with this release, set the workspace version and regenerate. `--check` refuses while anything is unstamped — the release pipeline runs it.

commands.name: confirm
commands.what: Put a person's name against a relation, after printing it and its source. `confirm --list` shows the ones with no name yet.

commands.name: ready
commands.what: Whether a person should be asked to look yet.

commands.name: codeowners
commands.what: Regenerate CODEOWNERS from the layer files.

commands.name: bundle
commands.what: `bundle verify` re-checks every published set's hashes. `bundle publish` publishes a new one, permanently.

commands.name: mutate
commands.what: Perturb a row's answer and require its own tests to notice; with --literals, move each decimal number in its hole code in turn and report the ones no test notices. Puts the row back.

commands.name: setup
commands.what: Point git at the project's hooks. Once per checkout.

commands.name: variables
commands.what: Write docs/VARIABLES.md — every variable, its unit, its range and why.

commands.name: run
commands.what: Evaluate a row and everything it needs. Always n ran, m blocked, with the blocked named. `--save` writes the run and its inputs as a result file; `--keep` keeps it in the results folder, once. A question already kept there is shown from its saved result; `--again` runs it anyway.

commands.name: sweep
commands.what: Sweep a declared input across a range. Refused points are recorded, never dropped. `--keep` and `--again` as for run.

commands.name: campaign
commands.what: The defaults, the saved case and each case file named, against one row.

commands.name: list
commands.what: The rows, with kind, owner and state.

commands.name: show
commands.what: A row's sheet, as the engine holds it.

commands.name: cases
commands.what: The case, how its inputs divide into customer and condition, and whether a case is saved.

commands.name: inputs
commands.what: Every input of the case as a CSV — group, id, value, unit, default and range — to fill in and pass back with --inputs. With --inputs, a file from an older version comes out in the current template.

commands.name: result
commands.what: A saved result shown as it was — nothing runs. Reads a result's folder, the CSV `run --save` writes, or the report page it rides in; `--html` writes that report, to send. Given a results file (.vleor), lists the results it holds.

commands.name: results
commands.what: Saved results, many in one file to send or keep: every result in the results folder, or the ones named. Each goes out whole, and every value again as a row that Python (`vleo.results`) or any SQL reader can ask for.

commands.name: results
commands.what: The results in a results file, put back in the results folder exactly as they were — nothing runs. A question already kept is kept once.

commands.name: figure
commands.what: The numbers one figure of the solar-weather record draws, as the JSON its panel reads — the same function as `/v1/figures/solar/<id>`, on the same bundle and saved case. From Python, `vleo.figure(id, **params)` returns the same as a dict. An unknown id or key is refused by name, with a failing exit status.

commands.name: selftest
commands.what: Check every fixture declaration in the tree is sound. `cargo test` executes them.

commands.name: data
commands.what: Fill the local reference-data store, say what is in it, or re-check its hashes.

commands.name: version
commands.what: The kernel, graph and build identity.

The numbers one figure of the solar-weather record states, worked out by the engine from the bundle it holds (`crates/vleo-modules/src/record.rs`): `density` — the correlation of F10.7 with Ap, their medians, the share of days below both, and the F10.7 deciles that saw a storm day; `storm-scale` — days a year at G1 to G3 in each cycle, the busiest cycle and the largest Ap in each; `kp-ap` — the daily Ap at each worst three-hourly Kp and where the published table sits above it; `recurrence-f107` and `recurrence-ap` — the autocorrelation of the detrended record against lag under three windows, Bartlett's band and the rotation's peaks; `spikes` — the F10.7 spike threshold, the spike days and bursts, and their rate per thousand days of cycle phase. `mean-cycle` takes `v` (f107, ap or ssn) and `bins` (2 to 100): every cycle stacked on phase, the mean of the complete ones, and how well the last two complete cycles repeat each other. `segments` takes `v` (ap or f107): the histogram and each band's share, banded by the rows themselves (`sw_regime`, `sw_activity_band`), and where the record crosses each cut; `regime-phase` — the share of days at each cycle phase `sw_regime` calls storm, and quiet. `climate` takes `v` and `by` (year, doy or month): the record's mean in each group on its own calendar, and the mean over its days; `smoother` takes `v`: each month's mean beside the 13-month smoothed value from `monthly_means.csv`, and what the smoothing removes. `growth` takes `v` and `by` (all or cycle): the signed change over leads from 30 days to 15 years at the 50th, 90th, 95th and 99th percentiles with the pairs behind each, or the 95th within each cycle. `forecast` takes `view` (lead, year or age): the issued 27-day outlook's skill against persistence — from the day before the issue, and from the issue date itself, which leaks — its bias and RMS error at each lead from 1 to 27 or in each year of issue on leads 1 to 14, with the pairs behind each; or the gaps between one issue and the next. `drivers` — the solar crossing's twenty-five scenario cells run on the saved case against the legacy tool's own run of them (`matlab/reference/mission_drivers.csv`): each ratio and gap, where each quantity's gap is widest, how many cells agree to a tenth of a per cent, and how far the worst is out. `thermosphere` takes `view` (solar, kp, slot or shape): env_exospheric_temperature run and probed as the panel asks — the three ways to raise the flux and their slopes, one Kp curve per scenario at its own flux with its two Kp readings and the widest gap, each scenario's two readings side by side, or the Kp sweep against the straight line its quiet end sets. `design` takes `v` (ap or f107): for Ap, with `g` (1 to 3) and `req` (l3_solar_req_03, _04 or _05), sw_storm_return_level swept over the mission duration, the G-level bound and the requirement, where the curve first reaches each, and the record's days at or above the bound in how many runs; for F10.7, with `reqf` (l3_solar_req_01 or _02), the four design-window rows and the analogue's peak swept the same way, the worst single day and what is left of the requirement above it, the window's width and where the peak first climbs above the hot single day. `closure` takes `pair` (01 to 05): the decision that spends that closure's margin fastest, by the levers' own ranking with the requirement skipped, the margin and the achieved quantity swept over it, and where each runs out. In these two the sweeps and the ranking run on the case the request carries, `set=` overrides and all, and each row's own answer — the requirement, the achieved margin — on the saved case, as the page's engine values are. The page draws them and computes none; an id the engine does not work out is refused by name.

Run, and keep what it returned and the inputs it ran on as a result folder: the parameters of `/v1/run`, and `label`; with `over`, `from`, `to` and `points` the sweep is kept with it. Kept once: a question already kept answers `already` and names it. Written outside the repository.
Keep a result somebody sent: `csv=` its CSV or the text of its report, and `sweep=` its sweep CSV when it is one. Kept once, as a save is.

Keep every result a results file (`results.vleor`) holds: `vleor=` the file, base64. Each is kept once, as a save is, pinned where the file says so; the answer names each one, how many were new and how many already kept.
Pin a saved result so every value is kept for good (`on=1`), or unpin it (`on=0`) so it is thinned to its summary once it is older than `VLEO_KEEP_DAYS`: `name`.
Remove one saved result: `name`.
Make a saved result's inputs the case: `name`. Checked like any case, and refused whole if one cannot apply.
A behaviour sweep, as `vleo sweep`. Refused points are reported with their reason. `reuse=1` and `again=1` as for `/v1/run`.
One relation at chosen inputs: `node`, and `in=<var>:<value>` for each. Answers even where a run would refuse a supplied value.
Which declared decisions actually move a row's answer, and by how much: `node`.
The largest fully-published branches a row is part of: `node`.

env.name: VLEO_CASE
env.what: Where the saved case is kept — the CSV the Inputs page and `vleo run` read. Outside the repository, so git never sees it. A copy made before a carry-over sits beside it.

env.name: VLEO_CONTRACT_RECORD
env.what: Set to `1` when running the contract tests, to record contract/examples/ again from the real engine after an answer's shape changes, and draft a schema for a route that has none. It never rewrites a schema. Unset, the tests only check.

env.name: VLEO_BASELINE
env.what: Set to `write` when running the test of today's answers, to record baseline/today.csv again after a deliberate change to the design, in the same commit as the change. Unset, the test compares and fails on any difference.

env.name: VLEO_BROWSER_ANSWERS
env.what: The file `tools/readers_check.py --answers` wrote: every answer the engine in a readers' page gave. Set when running `cargo test -- --include-ignored` in crates/vleo-kernel-wasm, it holds each of those answers to the same engine built natively, byte for byte. Unset, that one test refuses to run and says why; the pipeline's readers job sets it.
env.default: unset — the comparison is not run

env.name: VLEO_GOLDEN
env.what: Set to `write` when running the translator's golden test, to write the golden files again after an intended change to how methods are translated. Unset, the test compares and fails on any difference.

env.name: VLEO_LOG
env.what: Where a crash log is written when the tool hits a bug — one small text file per bug, naming the line of code; the newest 50 are kept. Send the file to whoever maintains the tool. Set but empty counts as unset.

env.name: VLEO_RESULTS
env.what: Where saved results are kept, one folder each — the Results page and `vleo run --keep`. Outside the repository. Point it at a shared or synced folder and everyone keeps one archive: each question is kept once, a question a colleague answered is shown rather than run again, and every result is written whole. Set but empty counts as unset.

env.name: VLEO_KEEP_DAYS
env.what: How many days a saved result keeps every value. When the daemon starts, an unpinned result older than this is thinned to its summary — the inputs it ran on, its answer, what could not run — and says so; a pinned one is kept whole for good. `0` never thins. A folder named by `VLEO_RESULTS` — usually the shared archive — is kept whole unless this is set too: thinning it is everyone's decision, not whichever laptop starts first. A value that is not a whole number of days thins nothing and says why.
env.default: 30; kept whole when VLEO_RESULTS names the folder

env.name: VLEO_ROOT
env.what: Where the daemon finds the web face, the tree and its pages. Unset, it looks upward from where it was started, then from beside its own program — which is how a kit runs with no checkout.

env.name: VLEO_DESIGN
env.what: A design file for the daemon to read the design from, in place of the one beside it or the folders of a checkout. A file that does not open stops the daemon, naming why: it never falls back to whatever folders sit beside it.
env.default: design.vleo beside the tool, else the folders

env.name: VLEO_PORT
env.what: The first port the daemon tries. It takes the first free one of sixteen from there.

env.name: VLEO_DATA
env.what: Where the local reference-data store lives.

env.name: VLEO_DAEMON
env.what: Where the checking scripts in tools/ find a running daemon.

env.name: VLEO_CHROMIUM
env.what: The browser the panel check drives, when it cannot find the installed one on its own.

cannot.what: Change a node — any field of its sheet
cannot.why: A change to the design has to be checked against every row that reads it, implemented, given evidence and released, so that everyone runs the same thing.
cannot.instead: Fill the node's form and send it to the developers. Check it first, on the Forms page.

cannot.why: A new node is a new folder in the tree with an owner, a place among its siblings and interfaces to rows that exist.
cannot.instead: The form for a new node, on the Forms page. A developer applies it with `cargo run -p xtask -- intake <form.html> --apply`.

cannot.why: Other rows read it. Removing one is a change to what every reader of it computes, and is decided in review, not in a form.
cannot.instead: Say so in the node's form, in its note. A developer decides, after `cargo run -p xtask -- reach` shows what reads it.

cannot.what: Move a node, rename it, or change its owner, layer, kind or order
cannot.why: These move the tree or change who reviews the row. Its identifier is also its folder and its variable name.
cannot.instead: Edit node.toml in a checkout, then `cargo run -p xtask -- gate`; the reason for each is under Reference.

cannot.what: Change a declared number in the design itself
cannot.why: A what-if and the saved case never touch the sheet: a declared value carries the name of the person who chose it.
cannot.instead: For your own runs, the case. For the design's default, the node's form.

cannot.what: Write the Rust in a step's slot
cannot.why: It is code: it has to compile, compose relations that already exist in the kernel, and be reviewed as code.
An expected value may never come from the code under test. A form may supply one; only a person records it, with its source.
cannot.instead: Edit fixtures.toml in the row's folder, with the value's source and provenance.

cannot.what: Put your name against a relation
cannot.why: Signing is an act of reading the relation against its source, done by the person who owns it.

cannot.what: Run the checks, the tests or the generators for the whole tree
cannot.why: They are what decides whether a change may be merged, so they run where the change is committed — and in the pipeline, on every push.
cannot.instead: cargo run -p xtask -- gate && cargo test

cannot.why: A published set is permanent by design, and every number checked against it depends on it not changing.

cannot.what: Show a figure, or click from a number to where it came from
cannot.why: The terminal prints the numbers — a row's, the chain behind each and every blocked row, and with `vleo figure` the numbers a panel draws; pictures are the browser's.
cannot.instead: The browser: the row's page, and the panels on layer 3.

fields.ask: what is this row called, in the tree
fields.why: the page title and every reference to it

fields.ask: what one question does it answer
fields.why: an equation with no question gets reused for the wrong thing

fields.ask: what does a reader need told that the question does not say
fields.why: the sentence under the question on the node's page, and the one place a row can say what it is NOT for

fields.ask: say it simply: what does this row work out, and why does it matter — in plain words, with no symbol and no word a newcomer would have to look up
fields.why: the first thing on the node's page. A reader who cannot yet read the relation reads this, and a writer who cannot write it has found a gap in their own understanding (docs/EXPLAINING.md, E2)

fields.ask: what is the relation
fields.why: the algorithm, and what a reviewer compares against the source

fields.ask: cited where — book, paper, page
fields.why: this is the claim everything else rests on

fields.ask: what is the answer's symbol
fields.why: the binding name in the generated signature

fields.ask: what quantity is it
fields.why: the signature; a dimensional error has to fail to compile

fields.ask: in what unit
fields.why: the conversion at every face boundary

fields.ask: what is the lowest value this row may return
fields.why: the guard the generated code refuses below, and half of what the gate calls this row's domain

fields.ask: and the highest
fields.why: the same, at the other end. The gate refuses a pair that is not ordered, so these two are decided together

fields.ask: why is the lower bound there
fields.why: a guard whose reason is not written gets deleted by the next person

fields.ask: why is the upper bound there
fields.why: the same, at the other end

fields.ask: which way does this requirement bind
fields.why: '<=' means the achieved value must stay under the bound, '>=' that it must reach it. Read the wrong way the closure still computes and still reports a comfortable margin, for a spacecraft that is about to be destroyed

fields.ask: what is the declared number
fields.why: a declared row computes nothing and publishes this, converted from the unit above. It is the whole of the row's content

fields.ask: why is it this relation and not another
fields.why: the relation says what; this says why, and it is what a reviewer reads before deciding whether to believe the number

fields.ask: how should the answer be read
fields.why: a number with no reading gets quoted out of context. This is where a row says what its answer does NOT mean

fields.ask: where does the simple version stop being true
fields.why: every simplification is wrong somewhere, and saying where is what makes it safe to use. Unwritten, the plain words get quoted as the physics (E4)

fields.ask: what do people commonly get wrong about this, and what is true instead

arrays.name: input
arrays.label: what this row reads
arrays.why: the consumer declares what it expects, and assembly refuses a mismatch against what the producer publishes. It is also the derivation graph: an input is an edge, and the edges are what decide what runs before what

arrays.name: algorithm
arrays.label: the steps
arrays.why: each step becomes one numbered hole in the generated model, and the hole is where a person writes the few typed lines that compose relations from the kernel. The step's text is the comment above it

arrays.name: theory
arrays.label: how the relation was arrived at
arrays.why: the expression says what the relation is; these say how it was got to. A relation an assistant invented carries a citation just as convincingly, and the derivation is what a reviewer reads instead of taking the citation's word

arrays.name: assumption
arrays.label: what has to be true for this to hold
arrays.why: an assumption nobody wrote down is one nobody can check. Each says what it assumes AND the case it fails in, because an assumption with no failure case is a sentence rather than a warning

arrays.name: risk
arrays.label: the risks this row registers
arrays.why: a risk is registered once, here, and moved only by node versions — a risk is reduced because something was tested, and the version that tested it is the record of how. Which risk-register row holds a risk says what kind it is

arrays.name: case
arrays.label: your test cases
arrays.why: inputs and the answer YOUR code gave, or that your code refuses them. They decide: the method is run on each one before you send the form, and the code the tool generates must reproduce every one before the node is connected to anything. At least three answers and one refusal

arrays.name: flight
arrays.label: flight software kept with this node
arrays.why: on-board code that implements this node, stored with its test beside the relation it implements, so the two are reviewed and versioned together
